nodes.claim: d-dimensional Euclidean Gibbs law; V in C2; 0<alpha<=beta; alpha I<=Hessian V<=beta I; 0<eta<=1/beta; exact joint Gaussian augmentation with X and Z independent.
Real Hilbert L2 equivalence classes; bounded operators; adjoint; self-adjoint order iff all real quadratic forms are nonnegative; unique positive square root from spectral calculus.
P is exact conditional expectation onto Y functions; reflection is law-preserving self-adjoint unitary; T=PUP on its range is self-adjoint contraction; L=Pperp UP; L*L=I-T^2.
Gamma=(I-T^2)^(1/2) is the unique positive root on the full macroscopic L2 space.
L*L=Gamma^2 and ||Lf||=||Gamma f|| for every macroscopic f.
rho=(1-alpha eta)/(1+alpha eta); gamma=sqrt(1-rho^2)=2sqrt(alpha eta)/(1+alpha eta)>0; delta=gamma^2=4alpha eta/(1+alpha eta)^2.
Conditional law p_y(u) and normalized conditional differentiation: gradient T f(y)=Cov(f(Y-),s_y(Y-)|Y+=y), initially Cc-infinity and then density/closedness.

Conditional Hessian >=(alpha+eta^-1)/4; score Lipschitz <=(eta^-1-alpha)/4 from beta eta<=1; conditional Poincare and Cauchy-Schwarz yield eta||gradient T f||^2 <= (1-alpha eta)^2/[4(1+alpha eta)] ||L f||^2.
Conditional potential has Hessian >=alpha+eta^-1; Bakry-Emery Poincare constant eta/(1+alpha eta).
Gaussian-smoothed marginal curvature >=alpha/(1+alpha eta), hence Poincare constant 1/alpha+eta; source route uses two-sided conditional covariance and log-density differentiation.
Tf belongs to H1 and 4eta||gradient Tf||^2<=||f||^2-||Tf||^2=||Gamma f||^2=||Lf||^2 for every L2 f.
nodes.boundary: Density and closedness are source proof ingredients, not public assumptions.

nodes.claim: T fixes constants and is self-adjoint, so preserves the orthogonal mean-zero subspace H_P,0. The mean-zero condition is membership, not an extra gap premise.
For centered f, Tf is centered, and ||Tf||^2=Var(Tf)<= (1/alpha+eta)||gradient Tf||^2.
Combining C2 and C3 then rearranging gives ||Tf||<=rho||f|| on H_P,0, including alpha eta=1.
||T||<=rho and -rho I<=T<=rho I on centered space.
Exchangeability plus Gaussian Poincare gives <g,(I-T)g><=2eta||gradient g||^2; using g=Tf and B13 yields (I-T)^2(I+2T)>=0 and spectrum T>=-1/2.
nodes.boundary: Independent branch needed by full B14/B17; not a dependency of the sharp B15 gap from C4.

nodes.claim: Gamma fixes the constant kernel at zero because (I-T^2)1=0 and Gamma is positive self-adjoint; it preserves constants-orthogonal H_P,0. Restriction Gamma0 is this SAME root, not a newly supplied operator.
nodes.boundary: This is a reconstructed standard consequence; not a separately printed source display.

nodes.claim: On H_P,0, Gamma0^2=I-T0^2 >= (1-rho^2)I=delta I.
For bounded positive self-adjoint A,B, B^2-A^2>=0 implies B-A>=0 by monotonicity of positive square root and root uniqueness; apply A=gamma I, B=Gamma0.
nodes.boundary: The source explicitly makes this square-to-root inference but does not print the monotonicity theorem/proof. This is a dependency to discharge, never a source binder or assumed hGap.

nodes.claim: Gamma0 >= gamma I in real quadratic-form/Loewner order, with gamma=2sqrt(alpha eta)/(1+alpha eta)>0.
Gamma0 is boundedly invertible on H_P,0 with inverse norm <=1/gamma. Positivity/order gives bounded-below; complete-space closed range plus self-adjointness/zero kernel gives dense range, hence onto.
nodes.boundary: The source asserts bounded invertibility. Its standard proof cannot be replaced by a public hOnto/hUnit assumption. Whole-space inverse fails since constants are killed.
